appliesTo: health benefit plan providers (insurers, HMOs, and utilization-review contractors) using AI in prior-authorization determinations

dutySources.human-review: § 1(b)(3) — 'a determination to deny, delay, or modify a request for prior authorization based on medical necessity shall always be made by a licensed physician or other health care professional who is competent to evaluate any recommendation or conclusion of artificial intelligence'
dutySources.disclosure-ui: § 1(c)(1) — 'Make prominent written disclosure regarding its use of artificial intelligence in utilization review in its policies and procedures.'
dutySources.impact-assessment: § 1(c)(2) — 'Ensure that its use of artificial intelligence and the outcomes that it generates are reviewed on a periodic basis to maximize accuracy and reliability'
dutySources.registration-filing: § 1(b)(2) — 'A health benefit plan provider shall certify annually to the department that the artificial intelligence used to make determinations of medical necessity on requests for prior authorization complies'

sources.humanReview: § 1(b)(3) — 'shall always be made by a licensed physician or other health care professional'
sources.decisionsCovered: § 1(b)(1) — 'uses artificial intelligence to make determinations of medical necessity on requests for prior authorization under health benefit plans'
sources.disclosure: § 1(c)(1) — 'Make prominent written disclosure regarding its use of artificial intelligence in utilization review'
sources.penaltyMax: § 1(d)(3)b.1 — 'Impose an administrative fine of not more than five thousand dollars ($5,000)'
sources.penaltyUnit: § 1(d)(3)b.1 — 'for a violation that occurred with such frequency as to indicate a general business pattern or practice'
sources.enforcer: § 1(d)(3)b — 'the department may also exercise either or both of the following disciplinary powers' (DEPARTMENT defined at § 1(a)(2) as 'The Department of Insurance of the State of Alabama')

flags: disclosure-ui is lossy here: the required disclosure is in the provider's written policies and procedures (§ 1(c)(1)), not an interactive user-facing label
§ 1(b)(1) sets a substantive decision standard (determinations must be based on the enrollee's medical history, unique clinical circumstances, and medical record) that fits no listed duty key
§ 1(b)(2)a–c certification content (no group-dataset reliance, fair/equitable application, no discrimination) fits no listed duty beyond registration-filing; it is an attestation, not a bias-audit

§ 1(c)(3) imposes a HIPAA-consistent data-use limitation ('patient data used in utilization review functions by artificial intelligence is not used beyond its intended and stated purpose') that fits no listed duty key

§ 1(c)(4) allows all (b)/(c) requirements to be 'satisfied by an attestation by an authorized representative... based on reasonable reliance upon internal policies, procedures, and third-party vendors'

penalty applies only to 'repeat violations' indicating 'a general business pattern or practice'; first finding yields a corrective plan (§ 1(d)(3)a), and the department may also suspend or revoke the certificate of authority (§ 1(d)(3)b.2) and require reimbursement of investigation expenses (§ 1(d)(4))
